entries.definition: spite and resentment at seeing the success of another (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Not simple wanting what another has: the gloss puts spite and resentment at the centre, so the ill-will toward the successful is the sense itself.

entries.definition: reprehensible acquisitiveness; insatiable desire for wealth (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same insatiable greed for wealth as *avarice*, but with a grasping, predatory force in the word rather than a hoarder's.

entries.definition: belligerence aroused by a real or supposed wrong (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same belligerence at real or supposed wrong raised to solemn weight — a word sized for a sin, where *anger* is sized for a mood.

entries.definition: overbearing pride evidenced by a superior manner toward inferiors
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A flat accusation: the swollen self-regard of *pride* has stopped being inward and is now overbearing, worn as a superior manner toward those it counts as inferior.

entries.definition: overbearing pride evidenced by a superior manner toward inferiors
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and chilly, naming the same overbearing pride as a bearing one carries above inferiors rather than levelling the blunt charge *arrogance* makes.

entries.definition: unreasonable and inordinate self-esteem (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Here the word is a vice and not a virtue - self-esteem grown unreasonable and past all proportion, and grave enough to stand as one of the deadly sins.
examples: Everybody is disgusted with his pride.
They had nothing to accuse him of but pride

entries.definition: plead or ask for earnestly
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Asking in a formal key, urged by earnestness rather than by *importune*'s wearing repetition.

entries.definition: call upon in supplication; entreat
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Raises the same entreaty to a pitch of desperation that *beg* states flatly.

entries.definition: beg persistently and urgently
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal, and the persistence lands as a burden on the person asked, where *insist* marks only the asker's refusal to stop.
examples: I importune you to help them

entries.definition: beg persistently and urgently
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pressing rather than abject - the force sits in refusing to let the asking drop, where *implore* puts it in the emotion behind it.
examples: She insisted and insisted until her father at last agreed to let her go.

entries.definition: call upon in supplication; entreat
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The entreaty in its most formal dress, an appeal made in the posture of supplication rather than *beg*'s bare asking.
examples: Pray forgive me, if I have been very presuming
and pray tell her from me, that she cannot expect to excel, if she does not practise a great deal

entries.definition: ask humbly (for something)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The humility is the whole of it, stated outright and with ceremony, where *beg* leaves the asker's lowness implied.

entries.definition: lure by imitating the characteristic call of an animal
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and technical here: the enticement is a mimicked animal cry, so the whole of the deception sits in the sound and none of it in any promise.

entries.definition: provoke someone to do something through (often false or exaggerated) promises or persuasion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Works by making the promise attractive rather than by baiting a spot, so the persuasion sounds pleasant even when it is the exaggerated kind.

entries.definition: entice and trap
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The enticing is only half of it — the closing of the trap is the other half, which is what makes this land harder than *entice*.

entries.definition: provoke someone to do something through (often false or exaggerated) promises or persuasion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Draws the person somewhere rather than merely dangling something, and of the three it keeps the falseness of the promise nearest the surface.

entries.definition: provoke someone to do something through (often false or exaggerated) promises or persuasion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest of the three: a promise held out to someone still standing free of it, where *lure* already has them moving.
examples: my friend Denny tempted me further by his account of their present quarters, and the very great attentions

entries.definition: (often followed by ‘with’) full of life and spirit
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Credits life and spirit rather than motion, and leans on a following 'with' to name whatever the thing is brimming over with.
examples: she was wonderfully alive for her age

entries.definition: marked by lively action
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Liveliness as vigorous springing action — sturdier and more robust than *bouncy*, which makes the same spring sound weightless.

entries.definition: marked by lively action
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The spring taken as a temperament rather than a feat — lighter and more playful than *bouncing*.

entries.definition: fresh and animated
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts freshness beside the animation, so the liveliness comes across as light and easy where *spirited* comes across as strong.

entries.definition: marked by high spirits or excitement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: High spirits or excitement caught in the act of rising — a thing in motion where *bubbly* names a settled quality.

entries.definition: full of or showing high spirits
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Covers both being full of high spirits and showing them, naming the outward fizz and the inward supply at once.

entries.definition: uttered with unrestrained enthusiasm
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Moves the fizz into the voice: enthusiasm uttered with nothing holding it back, warm but with an ear on the overflow.

entries.definition: uttered with unrestrained enthusiasm
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Names the quality of that unrestrained enthusiasm rather than a burst of it — looser and more casual than *burbling*.
examples: a novel told in burbly panting tones

entries.definition: marked by high spirits or excitement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The polished word for the same fizz — high spirits or excitement described with a formality the shorter members refuse.

entries.definition: marked by high spirits or excitement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The weakest approval of the fizz: the high spirits or excitement are granted, but froth lets them look light and easily dispersed.

entries.definition: full of life and energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain measure of the family — life and energy stated without a metaphor attached, so every other member here is a way of colouring it.
